one_line: Agent-ready accessible clinic booking page with holds and user-controlled confirmation.
what_it_does: Lets an agent search and temporarily hold clinic appointments while the person responds through accessible text, voice, buttons, or switch-like gestures.
leverage_rationale: Structured search and hold operations plus shared confirmation state materially improve reliability for users who cannot race a conventional booking form; a general UI-driving agent would be substantially less dependable.
leverage_evidence: About text describes WebMCP search, hold, release, and page-mediated questions.
Accessibility workflow includes scanning keyboard and non-typing responses.
execution_rationale: The concept and public demo claim a coherent workflow, but the packet has no submitted video despite referenced frame paths and the descriptive evidence is truncated, so end-to-end completion is only partially evidenced.
execution_evidence: Demo is reported alive and public repository exists.
About text describes a made-up clinic releasing appointments in waves and a three-minute hold.
impact_rationale: It addresses a specific, consequential accessibility problem in appointment booking and explicitly preserves user agency at the confirmation boundary.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets people unable to race booking forms.
About text explains switch, head-pointer, voice, and scanning-keyboard use cases.
creativity_rationale: Combining agent-mediated time-sensitive booking with multimodal accessible confirmation is a fresh and ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: The page lets an agent hold a slot but requires the person to decide through the page.
Gesture and scanning-keyboard interaction is integrated into a normal public booking page.
usability_note: Promising accessibility-first flow; actual usability is not fully observable from the packet.
red_flags: No video submitted and referenced frame evidence could not be independently inspected after vision service rate limiting.
advance_reason: High-impact, differentiated accessibility use case with meaningful WebMCP leverage.

one_line: Searchable Singapore/MAS regulatory registry with agent-accessible retrieval and comparison.
what_it_does: Provides a curated regulatory-intelligence interface where humans and agents search records, retrieve metadata and official sources, and compare requirements.
leverage_rationale: Structured search, retrieval, and comparison reduce the friction and ambiguity of multi-document regulatory research, though a capable browser agent could achieve much of the same outcome with extra effort.
leverage_evidence: About text names search_regulations, get_regulation, and compare_regulations tools.
The same underlying capabilities are presented to human users and agents.
execution_rationale: The packet clearly describes a focused MVP and claims an end-to-end live registry, but there is no video or frame evidence and the dataset is explicitly small and curated.
execution_evidence: Demo reported alive.
About text claims a deployed public site and three working WebMCP tools.
impact_rationale: Compliance and regulatory researchers have a concrete recurring problem of finding current documents and comparing requirements; the focused MAS/digital-payment-token scope gives the product credible niche value.
impact_evidence: Inspiration describes repeated manual PDF search and version comparison.
Product targets Singapore/MAS material relevant to digital payment token services.
creativity_rationale: It is a practical, competent application of WebMCP to regulatory research with a useful shared-interface angle, but the core registry/search category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Purposefully avoids a chatbot bolted onto a regulatory database.
Agent and human use the same registry capabilities.
usability_note: Focused workflow appears understandable; breadth and production depth are unclear.
red_flags: No video or submitted frame sheets; curated dataset limits demonstrated scope.
advance_reason: Useful and coherent but evidence is thin and concept is less differentiated than leading entries.

one_line: Deterministic factory decision lab for versioned human-agent replanning.
what_it_does: Lets an agent create bounded scenarios, simulate factory plans, compare immutable receipts, and recover safely when a human changes authoritative state.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central to a shared live state with explicit bounded writes, revision checks, atomic stale-write rejection, and receipt-backed simulation; generic UI driving could not replicate this reliably.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes six narrow tools over the same command path as the interface.
Stale factory revision is rejected atomically after human Packaging lock.
Visual frame sheet shows Factory Decision Lab and a completed six-tool WebMCP replay.
execution_rationale: The packet provides unusually detailed end-to-end evidence: two scenarios, constraint evaluation, human intervention, stale-write rejection, replanning, and infeasibility proof.
execution_evidence: Transcript gives concrete outputs including 11,114 units, cost-cap comparison, and 9,252 upper bound versus 10,937 target.
Frame sheet visibly shows product workspace and completed replay with six discovered tools.
impact_rationale: Factory planners and operations teams have a real coordination and decision-audit problem, and the product directly addresses authority, safety, and evidence quality.
impact_evidence: About text identifies fragmented dashboards, spreadsheets, simulation, and approval handoffs.
Demo mission uses explicit output, cost, machine, and defect constraints.
creativity_rationale: The combination of deterministic simulation, versioned shared state, stale-write safety, and proof of infeasibility is an ambitious and memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Human lock changes authority while preserving historical evidence.
System proves a conservative upper bound rather than merely recommending a plan.
usability_note: Dense operational workflow but clear phase and receipt framing; likely usable for its intended expert audience.
standouts: Atomic stale-write rejection and deterministic infeasibility proof.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage and unusually complete evidence of safe human-agent collaboration.

one_line: Governed product-truth graph that lets agents inspect claims and stage safe copy changes.
what_it_does: Classifies enterprise product claims against authoritative evidence, exposes provenance and authority boundaries, and allows local-only staged revisions without claiming production verification.
leverage_rationale: The structured domain contract—authority precedence, claim ceilings, provenance, deterministic gates, and shared focus—changes what an agent can safely reason about beyond visual UI automation.
leverage_evidence: About text describes seven imperative tools with stable claim IDs, schemas, and side-effect annotations.
Sandbox changes are explicitly capped and production verification remains separate.
execution_rationale: The stated workflow is coherent and intentionally bounded, with deterministic classifications and a staged-consistent terminal state, though no video evidence is supplied.
execution_evidence: About text names inspect, trace, stage, rerun, and non-issuing gate workflow.
Demo reported alive with public repository.
impact_rationale: Enterprise buyers and sales teams genuinely need consistent product claims across marketing, docs, contracts, runtime, and repositories; the tool addresses a costly governance failure mode.
impact_evidence: About text identifies drift across customer-facing and authoritative surfaces.
Workflow finds blocking claims for an enterprise sales gate.
creativity_rationale: Treating product truth as an inspectable, authority-aware graph with a strict claim ceiling is a notably original application of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Deterministic BLOCK/REVIEW/ALIGNED/NOT_EVALUATED classifications.
Refuses to call sandbox changes fixed.
usability_note: Governance concepts are sophisticated but the staged workflow appears deliberately explicit.
red_flags: No video submitted; visual execution claims are primarily textual.
advance_reason: Distinctive high-leverage governance product with credible audience value.

one_line: Creator-first comic studio with structured agent creation, context reading, and reviewable revisions.
what_it_does: Maintains a comic project’s story plan, character bible, storyboard, and visual identity while allowing agents to create or propose revisions for human approval.
leverage_rationale: Structured creative context and human-reviewed revisions give agents reliable access to a multi-part project model that would be difficult to reconstruct from UI scraping.
leverage_evidence: About text names create_comic, get_comic_context, and revise_comic tools.
Agent proposals appear as drafts and cannot silently overwrite the working copy.
execution_rationale: The product model and workflow are coherent, but no video was submitted and the packet gives limited direct proof of completed comic generation/export.
execution_evidence: Public repository and live demo are reported.
About text says tools connect to the same Studio project model and describes backend workflow infrastructure.
impact_rationale: Comic creators can benefit from agents handling structured production work while retaining authorship and approval; the audience and use case are clear.
impact_evidence: Creative state includes story, characters, storyboard, and visual identity.
Human creator explicitly decides whether to promote revisions.
creativity_rationale: A shared structured creative bible plus proposal-based agent collaboration is a fresh and ambitious take on comic production.
creativity_evidence: Creator-level tools operate on semantic comic context rather than button actions.
Human-in-the-loop promotion is built into the interaction model.
usability_note: Human review boundary is clear; visual production quality is not fully evidenced.
red_flags: No video; only one gallery image and limited end-to-end evidence.
standouts: Semantic creative context and non-destructive revisions.
advance_reason: Strong concept but less execution evidence than the leading projects.

one_line: Cinema seat selection based on modelled 3D sightlines rather than availability alone.
what_it_does: Lets users or agents browse Kolkata venues, inspect seat availability, and preview modelled eye-point views with distance, angle, clearance, and overall sightline ratings.
leverage_rationale: An agent can query venue and seat models and move the shared Three.js camera to a suitable seat, improving precision over UI automation, but the same recommendation is broadly possible with ordinary browser control.
leverage_evidence: About text describes five WebMCP capabilities for venue search, modelled seats, camera movement, and seat summary.
Seat metrics are structured and visible to the visitor.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a complete non-binding exploration flow and reports all five tools executed successfully, with multiple gallery images, but lacks video evidence.
execution_evidence: About text names six venues, date/time selection, availability, 3D view, and metrics.
Submission tagline states all five WebMCP tools executed successfully.
impact_rationale: Moviegoers, especially comfort- and accessibility-conscious visitors, have a real decision problem that standard seat grids do not address.
impact_evidence: About text explains distance, lateral offset, obstruction, and comfort concerns.
Non-binding preview preserves visitor control.
creativity_rationale: Turning seat booking into a spatial preview with modelled sightline quality is a memorable product angle, grounded in a specific cinema context.
creativity_evidence: Uses measured 3D eye points and forward-row clearance.
Agent request is expressed as a quality constraint such as a great sightline.
usability_note: The experience appears accessible and exploratory, with clear non-binding semantics.
red_flags: No video evidence; sightline claims are modelled rather than validated against real venues.
standouts: Spatially meaningful alternative to grid-based seat selection.
advance_reason: Good niche product and creative interaction, but WebMCP delta and evidence are moderate.

one_line: Autonomous product-engineering workflow from idea research through verified implementation.
what_it_does: Takes a natural-language idea through research, evidence gathering, repository discovery, architecture, approval, build, testing, verification, and learning.
leverage_rationale: The packet describes an agent-native software factory but provides little evidence of what WebMCP specifically changes versus a conventional orchestration platform or browser automation.
leverage_evidence: About text presents a long autonomous workflow and multiple model providers.
No concrete WebMCP tools or shared page state are described in the supplied packet.
execution_rationale: The claimed scope is very broad, while the packet supplies no frame sheets, video, concrete run output, or end-to-end artifact evidence; execution must be capped.
execution_evidence: Public repository and live demo are reported.
About text states intended stages but does not show a completed run.
impact_rationale: Software teams have real needs around research, architecture, implementation, and verification, but the submission does not demonstrate that this broad promise is delivered.
impact_evidence: Workflow addresses pre-coding research and evidence-backed engineering decisions.
Targets users who want ideas transformed into verified software.
creativity_rationale: The full idea-to-verified-product pipeline is ambitious and broader than a typical code generator, though the concept remains familiar in autonomous coding tooling.
creativity_evidence: Explicitly includes research, repository discovery, and approval before build.
Designed around multiple providers and local models.
usability_note: Scope and actual user flow are unclear from the packet.
red_flags: Very broad claims with no demonstrated central workflow.
WebMCP-specific behavior is not evidenced in the packet.
advance_reason: Insufficient WebMCP-specific and execution evidence for a credible advance.

one_line: Purpose-aware WebMCP evaluator that runs contract-based checks and records evidence-backed scorecards.
what_it_does: Evaluates target pages against declared purpose contracts, tool schemas, observable mutations, and runtime hygiene, then gives evidence and repair guidance.
leverage_rationale: Purpose contracts, selected checks, before/after evidence, and repeatable repairs provide a structured evaluation surface that is materially more reliable than an agent visually inspecting tools.
leverage_evidence: About text describes a local-first browser companion that discovers live tools and records schemas, annotations, timing, and evidence.
Prism itself exposes tools for reading contracts, switching profiles, running evaluations, and reading results.
execution_rationale: The design is coherent and evaluation dimensions are clearly specified, but no video was submitted and the packet does not show a completed target-page run.
execution_evidence: About text describes deterministic evaluation and repair retesting.
Demo and public repository are reported alive.
impact_rationale: WebMCP implementers need more than registration checks: they need proof that tools cover user purpose, mutate visible state, and respect approval boundaries.
impact_evidence: Targets commerce, project operations, content editor, and custom contracts.
Example repair addresses missing state revision and read-back checks.
creativity_rationale: Purpose-aware evaluation with journey-level evidence and repair loops is a notably stronger concept than a static WebMCP linter.
creativity_evidence: Contract includes intent, expected capabilities, and human-approved action.
Maps runtime evidence to purpose coverage, contract quality, mutation proof, and hygiene.
usability_note: Contract/profile model appears practical for developers, though the run experience is not shown.
red_flags: No video or frame sheets; no direct observed evaluation run.
standouts: Evaluates meaningful product behavior rather than merely tool presence.
advance_reason: Strong developer value and differentiated WebMCP evaluation model despite limited execution evidence.

one_line: Spreadsheet and CSV manipulation workspace intended to make cleaning and editing agent-accessible.
what_it_does: Offers spreadsheet/CSV operations such as filtering, deduplication, cleaning, and editing through a web application using ExcelJS, Next.js, shadcn, and WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: Spreadsheet actions are already amenable to general browser automation; the packet does not explain a structured shared-state or reliability advantage from WebMCP.
leverage_evidence: About text only states the product manipulates and edits Excel/CSV files.
WebMCP appears in the technology list without named tools or demonstrated agent workflow.
execution_rationale: The submission provides a terse description and no video or frame evidence, so core workflow completion and product quality cannot be verified.
execution_evidence: Live Vercel URL and public repository are listed.
About text names the stack but does not show behavior.
impact_rationale: Spreadsheet cleaning is a real productivity need for a broad audience, but the submission does not establish how well this product addresses it.
impact_evidence: About text identifies manual filtering, deduplication, and cleaning as the motivating problem.
Product explicitly targets Excel/CSV manipulation.
creativity_rationale: Spreadsheet editing is a familiar category and the packet offers no distinctive interaction or ambitious WebMCP angle.
creativity_evidence: Only the generic manipulation/editing premise is evidenced.
No novel workflow is described.
red_flags: No video, frame sheets, tool names, or end-to-end evidence.
advance_reason: Insufficient evidence and no demonstrated WebMCP differentiation.

one_line: Phase-governed room where humans and agents act through a changing WebMCP surface and append-only evidence ledger.
what_it_does: Runs a five-phase proceeding with phase-specific tool registration, commit/reveal mechanics, hash-chained records, server-observed verification, and explicit human ruling.
leverage_rationale: The page’s changing tool existence is itself the governance mechanism: agents receive only phase-valid capabilities, while shared ledger state, server verification, and human gates make generic UI automation materially inadequate.
leverage_evidence: Transcript and about text describe tools being registered/unregistered by phase via AbortSignal.
Commit/reveal uses hashes and nonce; ratification blocks on a human and records separate agent and host entries.
Video transcript explicitly reports outside-browser agent discovery and server-observed grading with honest fallback.
execution_rationale: The video transcript provides detailed end-to-end evidence across phases, including tool changes, ledger writes, reveal verification, refusal persistence, and limitations of browser attribution.
execution_evidence: 167-second video with transcript covering Open, Commit, Reveal, Ruling, and Closed behavior.
Transcript acknowledges when the page cannot distinguish a human click from an agent driving the browser.
impact_rationale: Governed human-agent proceedings and auditable decisions are a credible use case for organizations needing phase enforcement, provenance, and non-repudiable records.
impact_evidence: About text describes append-only SHA-256 hash-chained ledger and actor knowledge quality.
Human ruling and agent request are kept as distinct recorded acts.
creativity_rationale: Using WebMCP tool existence as a phase-enforced capability boundary, combined with cryptographic commit/reveal and honest evidence grading, is highly original and deeply pursued.
creativity_evidence: Phase advances remove tools rather than leaving always-present tools that reject calls.
Project explicitly builds around a missing native human-gate primitive and documents the workaround.
usability_note: The phase model is legible and conservative, though governed proceedings are inherently more complex than ordinary apps.
red_flags: Human-versus-agent browser click attribution remains inherently limited, and the project openly documents that limitation.
standouts: Honest server/client evidence grading and cryptographic ledger.
advance_reason: Outstanding WebMCP-native governance concept with strong demonstrated execution and honesty about platform limits.
